passages.section: Cell-layer fidelity: the Lean condition and Appendix B
passages.quote: Comparator accepts the three cell-layer theorems with Lean's kernel and four further checkers ([run 44819023135](https://github.com/wcook04/proof-reader/actions/runs/44819023135)); a diagnostic run with this readable file as the challenge stops at `Breakdown.AdjointDefect.transposeApply`, whose text matches the library but elaborates differently; see [the companion page](paper.md#5-checking-workflow-and-status).

anchor.heading: Cell-layer fidelity: the Lean condition and Appendix B

passages.quote: All seven fields read: positive period/weight, constant weight, closure of bounds harmonics under negation and flip, inclusion of zero and the reference-profile labels. They implement the stated harmonic set and symmetries (L3050–3057).

Partial correspondence. The top-level B.26 inequality and B.43 upper bound are identifiable. Full matrix entries and global-row representations remain unmatched. Exterior radius regularity/boundedness is explicit in Lean but compressed in the paper. See below.
Retained first-reading match. The enclosure conditions are repeated with the particular constants in `N` (L7033–7034); this is consistent with the existential enclosure in condition 1.
Retained first-reading algebraic match after substituting coercivity 3/50 and constant weight 39/50 (L7035–7036).
Retained first-reading match: the lower bound is `sqrt(1000·50/3)` (L7037 with L5200–5201).

Extended reading found the profile formulas, affine phase dependence, spline joins, origin/axis factors, pressure exponents, pressure-gradient correction and adjoint decay in the stated form. L2783–2903 and L3799–3920. The joins are essential to interpret classical derivatives as weak derivatives without singular interface terms.

Retained first-reading match of the expansion and far-field product bound. Open versus closed balls have the same integrals for the relevant measures; this does not remove the required measurability/integrability assumptions.
Retained comparison of the central and parameter-box errors and their combinations. Current source L6981–7000.
Retained match of the field identifications and `fitted_empty`. This emptiness reduces the generic fitted/free decomposition to the paper's B.53 expression.

**Partly comparable, with substantial extension.** The paper omits the precise coefficient format but states the analytic consequences. The formal shape conditions imply C¹/weak-derivative and decay properties sufficient for B.51. Full certificate-format equality cannot be established from the paper alone. L6720–6842, L6861–6890, L7007–7014 and the proof chain below.

The mesh permits a preliminary skeleton degree ≥−1; `IsCellModeLayouts` requires degree ≥1 on resolved harmonics (L4342–4347). Tested modes require ≥2 and volume degree ≥skeleton+2. Only azimuthal order zero is resolved on axis cells (L4681), as stated on p.57.

`ActuatorSupportFacts` L4832–4839 matches the intended cover of the forcing support when the chosen radius is nonnegative. It does **not** itself prohibit an empty mesh: at k=0 an existential radius −1 gives an empty square. This is a local observation, not a witness for the complete condition.

The first-reading comparison with B.19 and the classes of piecewise-polynomial weights is retained. The full coefficient lower-bound rules in `CoefficientConditions` have no fully written paper counterpart.

B.6–B.8 and the spline orders are represented explicitly by `reducedComps` and `IsTimeFieldData` (L2823–2903); compact fields have vanishing amplitudes and zero axis coefficient (L2905–2916). The first-reading Hermite data and support construction are extended by this formula reading.
`IsBoxUniform` L5011–5020 freezes the model and weight data across the parameter box, with the intended rotation-frame exception, consistent with B.1–B.2.

The former denominator `m²+1/4` is smaller for nonzero m. The new numerical obligation is weaker, requiring the sharper analytic bound. The current sources now have a successful build receipt; independent replay remains pending.

passages.section: Limits on claims of fidelity and nonvacuity
passages.quote: For example, `IsDirectionRadius` (L3456–3460) explicitly requires measurability, degree-zero homogeneity, a positive uniform lower bound and a finite upper bound; the paper compresses this as a radius depending on direction (p.59).
